title: Short NVDA via July 11 $190 Puts — Stop Day 2 Forced Exit; Reconstitution Premium Fully Absorbed
entry: Buy NVDA July 11 $190 puts when underlying trades $191–196 (NVDA at $193.85 June 30 open). Entry is most efficient in the first two hours of June 30 trading while the Stop Day 2 narrative is fresh and implied vol has not yet expanded into the puts. Do NOT initiate above $197 underlying — above that level the Stop Day 2 signal softens and the reconstitution exhaustion thesis loses its timing anchor. Position size: 8% of gross allocated to put premium (defined-risk structure; loss capped at premium paid).
stop_loss: NVDA daily close above $200 — above that level the reconstitution demand narrative is reasserting and the institutional selling supply overhang that overwhelmed the June 26 passive bid has been absorbed; exit immediately as the $190 strike loses intrinsic value rapidly above $200 underlying
targets: $188 underlying — institutional supply overhang persists into the first week post-reconstitution; NVDA tests the pre-reconstitution June 20 base; puts gain intrinsic value at approximately 0.4–0.5 delta; cover 40% of position

$182 underlying — OpenAI IPO delay extends beyond Q3 2026 timeline; AI hyperscaler capex tone turns cautious at a conference (Sievert/Jassy commentary); NVDA's Vera Rubin demand timeline is pushed; cover 40%

$175 underlying — structural AI capex pullback signal confirmed; sell-side begins cutting 2027 Vera Rubin revenue estimates; NVDA tests the May 2026 pre-reconstitution-announcement support; hold final 20% into July 11 expiry
risk_reward: 1:3.2 to third target (defined risk; underlying $193.85 to $175 = 9.8% downside; July 11 $190 puts priced approximately 5% of notional; full premium loss at stop vs ~3x at T3 if held into expiry with underlying at $175)
catalyst: NVDA's June 29 close at $194.97 triggered the Stop Day 2 forced-exit threshold ($195) from the reconstitution long trade, and NVDA opened June 30 at $193.85 — the second consecutive session below the key $195 level. The reconstitution bid — estimated at $200B+ in mandatory passive flows at the June 26 4 PM close — was overwhelmed by institutional selling. NVDA peaked intraday at $204.72 on reconstitution day (June 26) and has since given back every cent of the pre-positioning premium, closing June 29 at $194.97. This exhaustion pattern — where a known, large-scale mechanical bid fails to sustain a premium above the pre-bid level — is the clearest institutional supply signal in NVDA's 2026 trading history. The July 11 $190 puts (12 days to expiry) are positioned to capture additional downside as the supply overhang persists and the AI narrative lacks a near-term positive catalyst (OpenAI IPO delayed, no major hyperscaler conference until late July).
thesis:
The reconstitution failure is the primary signal. Every institutional participant knew the scale of the June 26 mandatory passive bid — $200B+ flowing into NVDA at the 4 PM window is not a secret. CTAs, active managers, and risk desks all had the same information and the same exit window. The fact that NVDA peaked at $204.72 intraday and then closed June 29 at $194.97 implies more than $10/share of institutional selling capacity at the $200–205 level — selling that overwhelmed one of the largest known mechanical bids in recent index history. Supply overhangs of this character typically persist for 1-2 weeks post-reconstitution as portfolio managers who were forced buyers at inflated prices now manage against their cost basis.

The AI narrative context amplifies rather than dampens the supply overhang. The OpenAI IPO delay removes the primary near-term catalyst for NVDA demand acceleration — when OpenAI's hyperscale compute expansion timeline is uncertain, the most direct validator of Vera Rubin volume is absent. NVDA at $193.85 trades at approximately 32x forward earnings, a multiple that requires Vera Rubin volumes to materially accelerate in H2 2026 to justify. Without a near-term positive catalyst (no major AI capex conference before late July), the multiple is exposed to downward revision from any negative AI demand signal.

The technical setup confirms the institutional reading: $195 was the Stop Day 2 threshold — calibrated precisely to the June 10 re-entry zone floor. A sustained close below $195 removes the last meaningful technical support above $188. The July 11 $190 puts are slightly out-of-the-money but gain intrinsically rapidly if the $188 support zone is tested in the first week of July. At $175 (T3), NVDA would be testing the May 2026 pre-reconstitution-announcement support at the intersection of the AI-capex discount and the reconstitution exhaustion discount.

The counter-party is the NVDA structural bull who argues the reconstitution pullback is a buying opportunity and the Vera Rubin cycle is intact: HBM4 demand confirmed by Micron's $50B Q4 guidance, and NVDA's next-generation Blackwell Ultra cycle adds another growth layer. These are legitimate arguments for the structural long — this position is not a structural short but a 12-day defined-risk play on a specific exhaustion signal with a specific expiry date. The premium at risk is capped; the position is not a naked short.
bull_case: NVDA reclaims $200 within 3 sessions as post-reconstitution dip buyers step in and the AI hyperscaler narrative holds. A positive Vera Rubin demand announcement or constructive commentary from a major hyperscaler CEO (Jassy, Altman, Nadella) resets the supply/demand narrative. July 11 $190 puts lose value as implied vol compresses and delta approaches zero. Loss limited to premium paid (8% of position). Exit with defined loss.
bear_case: NVDA sustains below $193 through the first week of July as institutional sellers who were forced buyers at $200–205 on June 26 continue to reduce exposure. T1 ($188) reached by July 7. PCE on June 25 (4.1%) has already removed the rate-cut catalyst — no macro positive offset available. OpenAI IPO delay confirmation produces additional AI sentiment selling. Puts gain intrinsic value at each target level. Full position covered at T3 $175 before July 11 expiry with the puts deeply in-the-money.
invalidation: NVDA daily close above $200; OR Vera Rubin demand announcement or hyperscaler capex acceleration commentary from Google/Microsoft/Meta/Amazon; OR July 11 expiry reached with NVDA above $190 (puts expire worthless); OR broader AI narrative reversal driven by a surprise positive catalyst (e.g., OpenAI IPO reinstatement with NVDA supply agreement)
